question.text: A bonus issue of shares is made:

answer.text: At a premium to market price
Without any consideration from existing shareholders, out of free reserves
By charging the face value to shareholders

explanation.text: The Logic: A bonus issue is made to existing shareholders without any consideration (payment) from them. The company uses its free reserves (built from genuine profits) to issue additional shares. The Trap: Bonus shares are free to shareholders — the company capitalises its reserves. A premium issue or a charged face-value issue would not be a bonus issue. Note: A company that has defaulted on debt repayment is restricted from making a bonus issue.
